```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
options(giotto.has_conda = FALSE, giotto.use_conda = FALSE, giotto.no_python_warn = TRUE)
```

GiottoConnect converts Seurat objects, AnnData (`.h5ad`) files and Bioconductor
SpatialExperiment / SpatialFeatureExperiment objects into Giotto objects with
three functions:

- `seuratToGiotto(sobject)`
- `anndataToGiotto("file.h5ad")`
- `spatialExperimentToGiotto(spe)`

All work the same way. They look at the structure of the input, pick the
bundled *mapping* that fits it (for example "Seurat v5 with an FOV image",
"scanpy/squidpy AnnData" or "SpatialExperimentIO layout") and build the Giotto
object from that mapping. Add
`source = "<directory>"` to get a Giotto object backed by a GiottoDisk project
instead of an in-memory one.

```{r}
library(GiottoConnect)
```

## Seurat to Giotto

As an example we load the small Xenium lung crop from GiottoData with Seurat's
own Xenium loader, and run the usual Seurat steps.

```{r seurat-load, results = "hide", warning = FALSE}
library(Seurat)

xenium_dir <- GiottoData::getSpatialDataset("xenium_mini_lung_ffpe")
s <- LoadXenium(xenium_dir, fov = "fov", segmentations = "cell")
s <- NormalizeData(s) |>
    FindVariableFeatures() |>
    ScaleData() |>
    RunPCA(npcs = 20) |>
    FindNeighbors(dims = 1:20) |>
    RunUMAP(dims = 1:20)
```

Convert it:

```{r seurat-convert}
g <- seuratToGiotto(s)
g
```

The Giotto object holds:

- the counts and normalized values;
- the control assays as their own feature types, named as Giotto's Xenium reader
  names them (`NegControlProbe`, `NegControlCodeword`, `UnassignedCodeword`);
- cell and feature metadata;
- cell centroids and segmentation polygons;
- the transcripts;
- PCA (with loadings) and UMAP;
- the kNN network `FindNeighbors()` built (as `kNN.pca`).

```{r seurat-parts}
GiottoClass::list_feature_info(g)
```

### On disk

With `source`, the same conversion writes expression, polygons, transcripts and
networks into a GiottoDisk project:

```{r seurat-disk}
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "xenium_from_seurat")
g_disk <- seuratToGiotto(s, source = project)
```

## AnnData to Giotto

`.h5ad` files are read directly from disk (with hdf5r); no python is needed.
GiottoConnect ships a small scanpy-style file to try:

```{r anndata-convert}
h5ad <- system.file("extdata", "mini_scanpy.h5ad", package = "GiottoConnect")
g2 <- anndataToGiotto(h5ad)
g2
```

From a typical scanpy/squidpy file the conversion takes:

| AnnData | Giotto |
|---|---|
| first integer matrix in `X`, `layers/*` or `raw/X` | raw expression |
| `X`, when it is not integer counts | normalized expression |
| `obs` / `var` (or `raw/var` for `raw/X` counts) | cell / feature metadata |
| `obsm/spatial` (or `X_spatial`, or `obs` x/y columns) | spatial locations |
| `obsm/X_*` | dimension reductions (`X_pca` with its loadings) |
| `obsp/distances` + `uns/neighbors` | kNN network (named from the space it was built in) |
| `obsp/spatial_connectivities` (squidpy) | spatial network |
| `var/feature_types` categories | one feature type per category |

For a large file, convert onto disk; the expression matrices are then streamed
from the file instead of being loaded into memory:

```{r anndata-disk}
g2_disk <- anndataToGiotto(h5ad, source = file.path(tempdir(), "from_h5ad"))
```

## SpatialExperiment to Giotto

`spatialExperimentToGiotto()` takes the layouts the Bioconductor readers
produce. Here the same Xenium crop is read with SpatialExperimentIO and
normalized with scuttle and scater:

```{r spe-convert, warning = FALSE}
library(SpatialExperimentIO)
spe <- readXeniumSXE(xenium_dir)
spe <- spe[, Matrix::colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(spe, "counts")) > 0]
spe <- scuttle::logNormCounts(spe) |>
    scater::runPCA(ncomponents = 20)

g3 <- spatialExperimentToGiotto(spe)
g3
```

The control probes that SpatialExperimentIO keeps as `altExps` become their
own feature types. PCA loadings and variances (scater's `rotation` and
`varExplained`) go with the PCA.

The bundled mappings cover:

| Input | Mapping | Converted on top of counts, metadata and reductions |
|---|---|---|
| SpatialExperimentIO (`readXeniumSXE()`, `readCosmxSXE()`, `readMerscopeSXE()`) | `spe-basic` | `spatialCoords`; altExps as feature types |
| VisiumIO (`TENxVisium()`, `TENxVisiumHD()`) | `spe-visium` | spot/bin positions converted from pixels to microns |
| SpatialFeatureExperiment (e.g. `readCosMX()`) | `sfe` | cell / nucleus segmentations, transcripts (`txSpots`), spatial graphs; control probes in the main matrix as feature types |

## Checking a conversion

Every converted object records what was done. `mappingProvenance()` shows the
mapping used, what each parameter was bound to, and what could not be carried
over, or was only estimated:

```{r provenance}
prov <- mappingProvenance(g)
prov$mapping
prov$losses[, c("part_id", "kind", "field", "note")]
```

`readbackCheck()` reads the source again and compares it with the Giotto object,
part by part. `MATCH` means identical, `DECLARED` a difference the mapping
announces (for example a unit that had to be assumed). `UNDECLARED` would mean a
real problem:

```{r readback}
rb <- readbackCheck(s, g)
table(rb$status)
rb[rb$status != "MATCH", ]
```

<details>
<summary>How a mapping is chosen</summary>

`findMapping()` profiles the object and lists every bundled mapping with its
status:

```{r find}
f <- findMapping(profileObject(s), ecosystem = "seurat")
f$candidates
```

Mappings are chosen by structure (an Assay5 with an FOV image, a Visium image,
a scanpy file), not by package version. When a part is stored somewhere else
than usual (for example coordinates in `meta.data` instead of an FOV), the
mapping's declared fallback is used, and `mappingProvenance()$alternatives`
says so. A mapping can also be passed explicitly: `seuratToGiotto(s, mapping =
"seurat-visium")`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Coordinates and units</summary>

Giotto uses `sdimx = x` and `sdimy = -y` for image-space coordinates (y pointing
down), so converted locations, polygons and transcripts are flipped in y.

- **Visium:** spot positions are converted from pixels to microns with the
  100 µm spot pitch (Visium HD: the bin size).
- **Others:** coordinates are taken as stored. Their unit is recorded as
  *estimated*, and the conversion warns when the coordinate range does not look
  like microns, for example scaled to [0, 1].

</details>

<details>
<summary>What is not converted yet</summary>

- Several samples or FOVs in one object: only the first FOV/image is used.
- Images and Visium scale factors.
- Seurat SCT assays.

Data that is present but not converted is reported as a warning when the
conversion runs, and declared losses are listed in `mappingProvenance()`.

</details>
